summary.text: Take \(n=7\). Since every allowed value of \(x\) is at least \(3\), the ordering \(x\le y\le z\) forces \(x+y+z\ge9\), contradicting the required sum \(x+y+z=7\); thus the strengthened representation claim already fails independently of primality.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
S=\{3,4,6,10,15\}.
\]
The conjecture is the conjunction, for every natural number \(n\), of the following two assertions:

1. if \(n>5\), then \(a(n)>0\); and
2. if \(n>6\), then there are positive natural numbers \(x,y,z\) such that
\[
x+y+z=n,\qquad x\le y\le z,\qquad x\in S,
\]
and all six numbers
\[
2x-1,\quad 2y-1,\quad 2z-1,\quad 2xy-1,\quad 2xz-1,\quad 2yz-1
\]
are prime.

We disprove this universally quantified conjunction by considering \(n=7\).

Suppose, for contradiction, that the conjecture were true. Since \(7>6\), its second assertion, applied to \(n=7\), would supply positive natural numbers \(x,y,z\) satisfying
\[
x+y+z=7,
\]
\[
x\le y\le z,
\]
and
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\},
\]
together with the stated primality conditions.

Membership in this finite set gives the exhaustive alternatives
\[
x=3,\quad x=4,\quad x=6,\quad x=10,\quad\text{or}\quad x=15.
\]
In every one of these cases, \(x\ge 3\). Because \(x\le y\), it follows that \(y\ge x\ge 3\). Because \(y\le z\), it likewise follows that \(z\ge y\ge 3\). Hence
\[
x+y+z\ge 3+3+3=9.
\]
On the other hand, the required sum equation says that \(x+y+z=7\). Combining these statements gives \(7\ge 9\), which is impossible.

Thus no ordered positive triple \(x\le y\le z\) with \(x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\}\) can sum to \(7\). In particular, there cannot be such a triple satisfying the additional primality requirements; those requirements never need to be examined. Therefore the conjecture’s “moreover” assertion already fails at the integer \(n=7>6\).

Since the original statement asserts that both clauses hold for every natural number \(n\), failure of the second clause at \(n=7\) makes the entire conjunction false, independently of whether \(a(7)>0\) or whether the first clause might hold. Consequently, the stated conjecture is disproved.
